title: A technology strategy needs a choice chain—not a project catalog
goal: Turn a platform problem into one explicit choice, a stop-list, and a small set of actions that reinforce one another.
tag: Distinguished Engineer · engineering strategy · coherent choices
concept:
A grocery list can contain bread, paint, and a train ticket. It tells you what to buy, but not what you are trying to accomplish. A project catalog has the same weakness: every item may be useful while the collection makes no strategic choice.

A usable technology strategy forms a choice chain. Start with a diagnosis of the important obstacle. Choose how the organization will respond. Name what will not be pursued now. Then fund actions that reinforce that choice. If a proposed project cannot be traced through that chain—or directly contradicts it—it belongs outside this strategy.
example: A data platform has five ingestion runtimes. Incident recovery varies from 20 minutes to 6 hours because each runtime uses different replay, ownership, and observability practices. The strategy is not “modernize ingestion.” The choice is: new regulated event streams use the managed event runtime; existing batch imports are not migrated this half. Coherent actions are a regulated-stream golden path, migration support for two high-risk services, common recovery evidence, and a stop on funding new custom schedulers.

use_case.when: Use a choice chain when several teams have more plausible platform work than capacity and need the same rule for funding, sequencing, and saying no.
use_case.example: A senior data-platform group must reduce recovery risk without pretending it can replace every Spark job, Kafka client, scheduler, and warehouse loader at once.
use_case.decision: Write a diagnosis, choice, non-goals, and reinforcing actions when work spans teams and tradeoffs are durable. Use an ordinary prioritized backlog when the goal is already settled and the remaining work is local execution.

practice: Switch among a project catalog, a diagnosis without a choice, a bounded choice, a coherent action set, and a contradictory investment. Predict where the chain stops and which proposal should be removed.
boundary: This is an original local coherence model, not Spotify's, Thoughtworks' or GitLab's strategy process. It tests traceability between five short fields. It does not estimate economics, political feasibility, migration risk, regulatory interpretation, capability maturity, portfolio dependencies, or whether the diagnosis is true.

questions: The platform lists six worthwhile modernization projects but never names the obstacle or tradeoff. What is missing?
More projects do not explain which obstacle matters or what the organization will decline.
Why does the example explicitly defer batch migration?
The non-goal protects capacity for the regulated-stream recovery choice
Batch systems can never be modernized
A non-goal permanently bans all later work
A time-bounded non-goal makes the current tradeoff visible; it is not a permanent technical claim.
A new custom runtime expands the exact recovery variation the strategy chose to reduce.

sources: Martin Fowler: Creating an integrated business and technology strategy
Foundation; published August 24, 2023. Warns that a current-to-future-state exercise can become a wish list and says strategy is as much about what is left out as included.
Thoughtworks: How to better connect strategy to implementation
Practice guidance; published January 23, 2026. Describes the failure mode where the strategy document becomes the goal and recommends operationalizing recommendations into roadmaps.
Spotify Engineering: AI Product Management at Spotify—A View From Three Angles
Recent primary case; published November 9, 2026. Says a promising architecture is not a roadmap and describes starting with a concrete problem, a useful test, and evidence for the next step.
visual_explanation: The strategy packet moves from obstacle to choice to an explicit not-now boundary and then to funded actions. The project catalog and diagnosis-only packets stop early; the contradictory packet turns red because one action expands the fragmentation the choice is meant to reduce.
written_questions: Take one current platform roadmap theme. What obstacle and organizational choice does it imply?
Name one attractive project to defer and one currently funded action that contradicts the choice.
